originalRequest: Produce the English variant of the shipped Chinese course learn-agent-orchestration (the series finale) for learn.agentmentor.dev. Teaching rewrite in English (not a translation): same 6-lesson structure, same lesson slugs, same interactive-block ids and answer positions, source quotes restored to their verbatim English originals from sources.md, runnable code kept logic-identical with only comments and user-facing strings translated, all review-era seam declarations preserved, cross-course references pointing at the live English course titles, natural desk-voice English prose with no AI-slop register.

briefCompleteness.evidence: The owner ratified the multilingual plan explicitly: all six locales on learn.agentmentor.dev, English first, batches of 2-3 courses in path order with a commit per course. The zh course is the verified source of truth for scope, learner model, structure, and grounding, so no additional clarification was needed.

learnerModel.targetReader: A developer who has finished the first eleven courses in this series, hand-writes the harness loop, and wants control flow in code — routing, fan-out, merge, and review across multiple loops
knownConcepts: Multi-agent division of labor and dispatch prompts (course 6)
Basic JavaScript / Node.js reading and writing
unknownConcepts: The workflow-vs-agent architectural distinction and the who-holds-the-plan axis
Chaining with programmatic gates; routing to specialized prompts
Parallelization variants (sectioning, voting) and bounded fan-out
Orchestrator-workers: model-decided decomposition under a code-enforced concurrency gate
The evaluator-optimizer loop and when it pays
Composing patterns into a deterministic orchestration script (this course's 'graph')
learnerModel.assumedEnvironment: A Node.js environment, terminal access, a text editor, and the course-7 harness code available to extend
learnerModel.firstIndependentAction: Take one oversized task from their own work and name which trigger (window, repetition, coordination) makes one loop insufficient
noviceRamp: Lesson 1 draws the workflow/agent line and the real triggers before any pattern
Lesson 2 turns the familiar single loop into a three-stage chain with gates, then adds routing
Lesson 3 adds parallelization with code aggregation and an explicit concurrency cap
Lesson 4 makes decomposition dynamic under orchestrator-workers with the four-element dispatch prompt
Lesson 5 adds the review loop and composes the patterns; lesson 6 upgrades the course-7 harness into the full deterministic script

learnerBrief: The target reader has finished the first eleven courses, writes the harness loop, and reads JavaScript. They can run one loop well; they can't yet put routing, fan-out, merge, and review around several loops with the plan held in code. The course gets them to place systems on the determinism spectrum, implement the five production-proven patterns as code, face the real cost ledger (90.2% gain vs 15x tokens, capped concurrency, dispatch-prompt discipline), and upgrade their own harness into a deterministic orchestration script with a step-by-step audit trail.
scope: Covered: workflow vs agent and who-holds-the-plan, chaining with gates, routing, parallelization (sectioning and voting) with bounded fan-out and pass-references-not-payloads merging, orchestrator-workers with four-element dispatch prompts, the evaluator-optimizer loop, pattern composition as this course's 'graph' metaphor, and a hands-on deterministic orchestration script over the course-7 harness. Not covered: third-party orchestration frameworks (LangGraph et al. unmentioned), multi-agent collaboration principles (course 6), workflow concepts and diagramming (course 2). Depth: from one loop to a readable, runnable, re-runnable orchestration script.

qualitySelfReview.diagramUse: Diagrams are kept exactly where the zh original uses them — most importantly the composition diagram in lesson 5 whose topology (including the gate node and the classification-as-model-call classification) was review-validated; labels rewritten in English, topology untouched. No diagrams added or removed.
weakestPoints: The 'graph' is explicitly this course's own engineering metaphor, not official vocabulary — the text says so wherever it leans on the term, and reviewers must keep that honesty intact
The 90.2%/15x figures are one production system's reported numbers under its own eval, framed as such rather than as constants

The capstone deliberately builds a VARIANT of lesson 5's graph with all differences declared in a reconciliation table rather than code-unified — a reader skimming past the table may miss that the naming differs by declaration, not by accident

As an English teaching rewrite of a verified zh course, idiomatic drift is the residual risk: source quotes were restored verbatim and code kept logic-identical, but prose was re-taught rather than translated, so review must check meaning-equivalence against the zh lessons
followUpChecks: Render pass on learn.agentmentor.dev /en/agent-orchestration/... after deploy: all 6 lessons plus README, interactive cards hydrate
Verify every glossary term appears verbatim in the en lessons (attach check)
Verify every [^Sn] anchor in en lessons has a matching ## Sn block in en sources.md
Confirm the six check-block ids and correct-answer positions are byte-identical to zh (b/c/a/b/c/a in lesson order)
Re-run the three scripts (chain, fanout, orchestrate) and confirm the POOL_SIZE=0 guard, exit codes (crash 3 / needs_human 1), STOP_AFTER-only-merge behavior, and pasted outputs all match

acceptanceReview.terminalTask: The learner can upgrade a single-loop harness into a deterministic orchestration script — route, fan out three workers under a code-enforced pool, merge by references, run a review loop that returns the best draft, report with an audit trail — and reconcile it line by line against the promises the earlier lessons and courses made.
acceptanceReview.interactionCheck: Six agentmentor-check blocks, one per lesson (bigger-window in L1, chain-vs-one-prompt in L2, unbounded-fanout in L3, vague-dispatch in L4, graph-is-ours in L5, llm-as-glue in L6), preserved from the zh variant with identical ids, modes, choice counts, and correct-answer positions; label, prompt, whyHere, choice text, and feedback are English teaching rewrites specific to each lesson's misconception. Exercises keep the zh Level structure with rubric, answer, and hints per Level.
acceptanceReview.learnerFitCheck: The course assumes the prior eleven courses: the harness loop, dispatch prompts, evals, and observability. The determinism axis, gates, bounded fan-out, dynamic decomposition, and the review loop are taught from zero in dependency order; the learner first assembles the full script in lesson 6, after every prerequisite. Lesson 1's first exercise asks only for a which-trigger judgment on the reader's own oversized task.
promotionNotes: English variant of a shipped zh course: structure, grounding, and answer positions inherited from the verified original

All source quotes restored to verbatim English originals and checked byte-exact against sources.md

The capstone's declared-variant reconciliation table (stop-field renames, rounds semantics, observability differences, orchestrator-workers unimplemented) preserved in English — declared, never silently code-unified

memoryBoundary: This agentmentor.json is a course-local state record, stored only in the course directory for quality checks and learning-path tracking. It is never written back to Claude Code or any host AI system's long-term memory and does not affect other courses or conversations.
